chapters.title: Why RAG hits the latency wall
Static vs. liquid context and Work IQ
The service account trap and stalled Copilot pilots
Entra Agent ID and policy as code
Reasoning traces, anomaly detection and Work IQ
A2A vs. MCP and agent density
Consumption billing, reasoning ROI and FinOps
Multi-cloud governance, rollout and why most agents fail

takeaways: RAG works for static documents, but agents that act need live organizational context, which Work IQ provides by reasoning over Microsoft 365 data in place.
Shared service accounts cannot be governed; Entra Agent IDs, policy as code, reasoning traces and Defender monitoring make agents accountable first-class identities managed through Agent 365.

Consumption billing in Copilot Credits makes reasoning efficiency a cost issue, so organizations need FinOps for AI, a staged pilot-to-production path and the discipline to retire agents that do not deliver.
hook: Many organizations think they are transforming with AI but are really just deploying chat interfaces over search. This episode shows architects and IT leaders how Work IQ, Agent 365, Entra Agent ID and the A2A protocol form an agentic operating model, and what it really costs in governance, identity and Copilot Credits.
